sections.content: When rules conflict, specificity decides: inline > id > class/attribute/pseudo-class > element/pseudo-element. !important overrides everything (avoid it).
The cascade layers (later rules win at equal specificity), origin (author vs user agent), and inheritance complete the picture.
Key points: count (ids, classes, elements), .a.b.c beats #id? No — any id beats all classes; equal specificity → source order wins.

sections.codeExample:
#nav .link { color: red; }
.link { color: blue; }  /* red wins: higher specificity */
